You are gentle_otter27, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. <collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll first inspect the bundled docs, the executable’s CLI surface, and our group feed so I can align with existing coverage and claim a useful area.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). [`tar`]: https://www.gnu.org/software/tar/ [infozip]: http://www.info-zip.org/ "}}

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /workspace/compress_impl.py
@@
         if p.is_dir():
             result.append((p, p.name))
             for root, dirs, files in os.walk(p, followlinks=follow):
                 dirs.sort(); files.sort()
                 rp=Path(root)
-                result.extend((rp/d, str((rp/d).as_posix())) for d in dirs)
-                result.extend((rp/f, str((rp/f).as_posix())) for f in files)
+                # Paths inside an archive are relative to the supplied directory,
+                # even when that directory was given by an absolute filesystem path.
+                result.extend((rp/d, (p.parent / (rp/d)).relative_to(p.parent).as_posix()) for d in dirs)
+                result.extend((rp/f, (p.parent / (rp/f)).relative_to(p.parent).as_posix()) for f in files)
*** End Patch";

@@

+def decompress_stdin(data: bytes, fmt: str, output_dir: str|None=None) -> tuple[str,list[tuple[str,int]]]:
+    """Decompress stdin using the explicit format, writing plain data to ouch-output."""
+    exts = [x.lower().lstrip(".") for x in fmt.split(".") if x]
+    aliases = {"tgz": ["tar", "gz"], "tbz": ["tar", "bz"], "tbz2": ["tar", "bz2"],
+               "txz": ["tar", "xz"], "tlzma": ["tar", "lzma"], "cbt": ["tar"],
+               "cbz": ["zip"], "epub": ["zip"]}
+    if len(exts) == 1 and exts[0] in aliases:
+        exts = aliases[exts[0]]
+    if not exts:
+        raise ValueError("missing format")
+    decoded=data
+    for ext in reversed(exts):
+        if ext in ("gz",): decoded=gzip.decompress(decoded)
+        elif ext in ("bz", "bz2"): decoded=bz2.decompress(decoded)
+        elif ext == "xz": decoded=lzma.decompress(decoded)
+        elif ext == "lzma": decoded=lzma.decompress(decoded, format=lzma.FORMAT_ALONE)
+        elif ext in ("tar", "zip"):
+            break
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"unsupported format: {ext}")
+    root=Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else Path("ouch-output")
+    if exts[0] in ("tar", "zip"):
+        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+        if exts[0] == "zip":
+            with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(decoded)) as zf: entries=_extract_zip(zf,root)
+        else:
+            with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(decoded),mode="r:*") as tf: entries=_extract_tar(tf,root)
+        return str(root),entries
+    # When an explicit stream format ends in a bundled archive, extract it.
+    if decoded.startswith((b"PK\x03\x04",b"PK\x05\x06")):
+        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(decoded)) as zf: entries=_extract_zip(zf,root)
+        return str(root),entries
+    if len(decoded)>262 and decoded[257:262]==b"ustar":
+        root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(decoded),mode="r:*") as tf: entries=_extract_tar(tf,root)
+        return str(root),entries
+    path=(Path(output_dir)/"ouch-output") if output_dir is not None else Path("ouch-output")
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_bytes(decoded)
+    return str(path),[(str(path),len(decoded))]
*** End Patch";

from pathlib import Path

ALIASES = {
    "tgz": ("tar", "gz"), "tbz": ("tar", "bz"), "tbz2": ("tar", "bz2"),
    "txz": ("tar", "xz"), "tlzma": ("tar", "lzma"), "tlz4": ("tar", "lz4"),
    "tsz": ("tar", "sz"), "tzst": ("tar", "zst"), "tlz": ("tar", "lz"),
    "cbt": ("tar",), "cbz": ("zip",), "epub": ("zip",), "cb7": ("7z",),
}

def formats_for(path, fmt=None):
    if fmt:
        data[pos+148:pos+156]=f"{checksum:07o}\0".encode()
        pos += 512 + ((member_size + 511) // 512) * 512
    return bytes(data)

def compress(inputs, output, *, fmt=None, level=None, fast=False, slow=False, follow=False, quiet=False, hidden=False, gitignore=False):
    """Create output; returns (success, message)."""
    fmts=formats_for(output, fmt)
    supported={"tar","zip","gz","bz","bz2","xz","lzma","bz3","lz4","lz","sz","zst","rar","7z"}
    aliases=set(ALIASES)
    if fmt and any(f not in supported and f not in aliases for f in fmts):
        bad=next(f for f in fmts if f not in supported and f not in aliases)
        return False, f"[ERROR] Failed to parse `--format {fmt}`\n - Unsupported extension '{bad}'\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z\nhint: Supported aliases are: tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr\nhint: \nhint: Examples:\nhint:   --format tar\nhint:   --format gz\nhint:   --format tar.gz"
    if not fmts or (not fmt and any(f not in supported and f not in aliases for f in fmts)):
        return False, f'[ERROR] Cannot compress to "{output}"\n - You must supply the compression format\n\nhint: Try adding supported extensions (see --help):\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.tar.gz\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.zip\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can overwrite this option by using the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output} --format tar.gz'
    if any(f not in {"tar","zip","gz","bz","bz2","xz","lzma"} for f in fmts):
        bad=next(f for f in fmts if f not in {"tar","zip","gz","bz","bz2","xz","lzma"})
        return False, f'[ERROR] Unsupported extension "{bad}"'
    if "tar" in fmts[1:]:
        return False, "[ERROR] File extensions are invalid for operation\n - The archive extension '.tar' can only be placed at the start of the extension list\n\nhint: You can use `--format` to specify what format to use, examples:\nhint:   ouch compress file.zip.zip file --format zip\nhint:   ouch decompress file --format zst\nhint:   ouch list archive --format tar.gz"
    if "zip" in fmts[1:]:
        return False, "[ERROR] File extensions are invalid for operation\n - The archive extension '.zip' can only be placed at the start of the extension list\n\nhint: You can use `--format` to specify what format to use, examples:\nhint:   ouch compress file.zip.zip file --format zip\nhint:   ouch decompress file --format zst\nhint:   ouch list archive --format tar.gz"
    is_folder = any(Path(source).is_dir() for source in inputs)
    if fmts[0] not in ("tar", "zip") and (len(inputs)>1 or is_folder):
        f=fmts[0]
        shown = os.path.relpath(output, os.getcwd())
        target = str(Path(output).with_suffix("")) + f".tar.{f}"
        description = "a folder" if is_folder else "multiple files"
        return False, f'[ERROR] Cannot compress to "{shown}"\n - You are trying to compress {description}.\n - The compression format \'{f}\' does not accept multiple files.\n - Formats that bundle files into an archive are tar, zip and 7z.\n\nhint: Try inserting \'tar.\', \'zip.\' or \'7z.\' before \'{f}\'.\nhint: From: "{shown}"\nhint: To:   "{target}"'

def detect_format(filename: str) -> str|None:
    """Infer a common archive codec from its file signature."""
    data=Path(filename).read_bytes()[:512]
    if data.startswith(b'\x1f\x8b'): return 'gz'

def _tar(inputs, follow=False, hidden=False, gitignore=False):
    buf=io.BytesIO()
    def normalize(info):
        info.uname = ""
        info.gname = ""
        if info.isdir():
            info.name = info.name.rstrip("/")
        return info
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=buf, mode="w", format=tarfile.USTAR_FORMAT, dereference=follow) as tf:
        for p, arc in _collect(inputs, follow, hidden, gitignore):
            if not p.is_symlink() or follow:
                tf.add(p, arcname=arc, recursive=False, filter=normalize)
            else:
                info=tarfile.TarInfo(arc); info.type=tarfile.SYMTYPE; info.linkname=os.readlink(p); info.mode=0
                tf.addfile(info)
        content_end=tf.offset
    data=bytearray(buf.getvalue())
    # The reference writer terminates at the two mandatory zero blocks instead
    # of padding every archive to tarfile's 10 KiB record boundary.
    data=data[:content_end+1024]
    # ouch's tar writer uses GNU-style type bits in the mode field and the
    # traditional blank uname/gname and device fields.
    pos=0
    while pos < content_end:
        block=data[pos:pos+512]
        if not any(block):
            break
        try: member_size=int(bytes(block[124:136]).rstrip(b"\0 ") or b"0",8)
        except ValueError: member_size=0
        kind=block[156]
        if kind == ord("5"):
            name=bytes(block[:100]).split(b"\0",1)[0]
            if name.endswith(b"/"):
                data[pos:pos+100]=(name[:-1]+b"\0").ljust(100,b"\0")
        try: mode=int(bytes(block[100:108]).rstrip(b"\0 ") or b"0",8)
        except ValueError: mode=0o644
        if kind in (0, ord("0")): kindbits=0o100000
        elif kind == ord("5"): kindbits=0o040000
        elif kind == ord("2"): kindbits=0; mode=0
        elif kind == ord("1"): kindbits=0o100000
        else: kindbits=0
        data[pos+100:pos+108]=f"{kindbits | mode:07o}\0".encode()
        data[pos+257:pos+265]=b"ustar  \0"
        data[pos+329:pos+337]=b"0000000\0"
        data[pos+337:pos+345]=b"0000000\0"
        data[pos+148:pos+156]=b"        "
        checksum=sum(data[pos:pos+512])
        data[pos+148:pos+156]=f"{checksum:07o}\0".encode()
        pos += 512 + ((member_size + 511) // 512) * 512
    return bytes(data)

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Proceeding with `{detected}` that was detected from the file signature.' if opts.get("no"): print(warning, file=sys.stderr) return False if opts.get("yes"): print(warning, file=sys.stderr) return True question = f'Do you want to decompress \'"{shown}"\'?' print(question, file=sys.stderr) if not sys.stdin.isatty(): print("Stdin is null, can't read user input (bypass with --yes, but be careful)", file=sys.stderr) return None print(question + " [Y/n] ", end="", file=sys.stderr, flush=True) answer = sys.stdin.readline().strip().lower() if answer in ("n", "no"): return False if answer in ("y", "yes"): print(warning, file=sys.stderr) return True print("Stdin is null, can't read user input (bypass with --yes, but be careful)", file=sys.stderr) return None def main(argv=None): argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv) accessible_env = os.environ.get("ACCESSIBLE") if (accessible_env is not None and accessible_env not in ("true", "false") and "--help" not in argv and "-h" not in argv and argv[:1] != ["help"]): print(f"error: invalid value '{accessible_env}' for '--accessible'\n [possible values: true, false]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.", file=sys.stderr) return 2 if not argv: sys.stderr.write(help_text("short"));
